subject: Post-call: Tidal POC visibility map + eval-harness next steps
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@tidal.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-07-22T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: Tidal POC visibility map + eval-harness next steps

Samir — thanks for the call this morning. Short recap and proposed next steps so we have a single plan to share with your engineering leads.

Key goals for the 3-week POC (as we discussed):
- Validate production latency at 95th pct under your steady-state load (250 rps).
- Confirm end-to-end cost per 1k responses with Redwood Dedicated vs hosted baseline.
- Prove observability and alerting for the three SLIs below across your staging environment.

Suggested SLIs / signals to instrument for acceptance:
1) Token latency P95 (per-request) — target: <1200ms after warmup
2) Error rate (5xx / timeouts) — target: <0.5% over 24h windows
3) Model quality regressions — automated prompt-suite pass rate >= 92%

Minimum telemetry we need from your side:
- Exported application logs (stdout) with request_id and model_variant tags
- Traces for request lifecycle (ingest -> routing -> inference) with span durations
- Basic metrics: token_count, request_latency_ms, inference_gpu_utilization_sample

Owners & timeline (proposed):
- Redwood infra hookup and Grafana dashboard: Marissa (week 1)
- Tidal log export + trace sampling config: Samir / ops@tidal.ai (week 1)
- Eval harness & prompt suite run: Sergio (weeks 1–2)
- Acceptance run and handoff: Ben (week 3)

Attachments: poc-success-metrics.xlsx (proposed pass/fail matrix), grafana-lite-dash.json (starter dashboard). I uploaded both to the shared Drive link below.

Next actions:
1) Samir — confirm owners on your side and the staging cluster details (k8s namespace, log sink endpoint, and whether you can send OTLP traces).
2) Marissa — if you can spin the starter dashboard and share the Grafana link, we'll iterate.
3) Sergio — prepare the evaluation prompt set and smoke tests; include automated quality checks.

I'll follow up to schedule a 30-minute kickoff for Monday to walk through the dashboard and log schema.

Thanks,
Ben
Director, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

—Samir

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Samir Patel <samir@tidal.ai>
Date: 2027-07-24T15:37:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Tidal POC visibility map + eval-harness next steps

Quick update from the evaluators' side — I've sketched the eval-harness plan and the acceptance checklist. High level:
- Week 1: Instrumentation & smoke tests (logs/traces flowing, starter dashboard visible). Owner: Samir + Marissa.
- Week 2: Full prompt-suite runs (automated) across variants; capture pass/fail and diff for quality regression detection. Owner: Sergio.
- Week 3: Load soak and cost comparison (steady 250 rps, then 1-hour spike at 400 rps). Owner: Ben + Laura.

Acceptance checklist (must pass all to sign off):
- Traces show end-to-end request latencies and span breakdowns (ingest, routing, model_infer).
- Logs include request_id and model_variant for >99% of entries.
- P95 token latency <1200ms during 95% of sampling windows.
- No quality regression: automated prompt-suite pass rate >= 92% across main intents.
- Cost per 1k responses within 15% of Redwood forecast.

For the prompt-suite output, JSON array is best. Example record: {"request_id":"...","prompt_id":"...","variant":"v1","pass":true,"score":0.93}. Samir — can Tidal's runner emit that structure? If not, we can transform CSV to this format in the harness.

Laura — can you take point on the load soak scheduling and confirm whether we should do the 400 rps spike on Tuesday morning (07:00–08:00 PT) or Thursday? I'll coordinate the runbook and rollback plan.

Thanks all — I'll upload the lightweight harness and a Readme to the Drive folder by EOD so your teams can review.

—Sergio
Principal Applied ML Engineer, Redwood Inference
